metadata.title: The relationship between student engagement and dropout risk in early adolescence
metadata.venue: International Journal of Educational Research Open

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study used a questionnaire-based design administered in groups to grade 7 students, teachers, and school heads in 117 Hungarian primary schools, with an analytic subsample defined by missingness handling (listwise deletion). The manuscript does not report the use of any complex survey design weights (e.g., student sampling weights) or replicate-weight procedures, and it does not describe any weight variable names. Because the analysis relies on standard regression and structural equation/path modeling rather than ILSA-style population inference, the results should be interpreted as associations within the targeted at-risk school regions rather than nationally representative estimates. The only explicit preprocessing step affecting the analytic sample is the exclusion of cases with missing data (no imputation in the SEM models).

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible Values are not applicable because the dependent variable is not an ILSA cognitive achievement score generated via PVs; instead, the study uses self-reported grade point average (GPA) and self-reported engagement indicators from a locally administered questionnaire. The paper also does not use PV-based scaling or IRT/WLE theta scores as outcomes. Therefore, PV handling is structurally irrelevant to this dataset and measurement approach.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The fall 2020/2021 questionnaire-based study included 5975 seventh-grade students across 117 Hungarian primary schools, of whom 3251 completed the electronic questionnaire. The paper states that due to missing data and the use of listwise deletion, the final analytic sample for the study was N=3230. For the SEM/path models, the complete database contained 3230 individuals, but only 2124 cases had all variables available; missing data were not imputed for these models, and the SEM/path analyses used N=2124.

main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using TIMSS the study leveraged Affective engagement index, Teacher-student relationships, Family support for learning to predict Primary study outcome (heuristic migration), finding that This study used a locally administered questionnaire study in Hungary (fall 2020/2021) with grade 7 students from 117 at-risk primary schools (initial N=5975; analytic N=3230 after listwise deletion; SEM/path models used N=2124 with complete cases). The dependent variable was students’ self-reported grade point average (GPA) from the previous academic year, treated as a continuous achievement indicator, while student engagement was measured using an adapted Student Engagement Instrument (SEI) covering affective, cognitive, behavioral, and academic engagement dimensions. The authors estimated associations using Pearson correlations and linear regression, and tested hypothesized mediation/hierarchy using structural equation modeling and path analysis (SPSS AMOS 27). In regression, the comprehensive model explained 41% of GPA variance (Adjusted R²=0.41), with the strongest effects from failure/grade repeat (B=-0.794) and homework completion (B=0.106), alongside maternal education (B=0.099). The hypothesized mediation model was not supported, with poor model fit (e.g., structural model CFI=0.47, RMSEA=0.17), and the authors note potential common-method variance due to self-report measures. Limitations include non-representative sampling of at-risk regions and no imputation for missing variables in SEM. This indicates that these patterns have implications for educational policy and instructional practice, though cross-sectional ILSA designs cannot establish causality.

data.null_fields_interpretation: This is not an empirical machine-learning prediction paper: the analysis uses correlations, linear regression, and structural equation/path modeling (SEM/AMOS) rather than training ML algorithms. Consequently, there are no ML techniques to extract and no ML target-variable performance metrics (e.g., accuracy/AUC/RMSE from predictive models). The study’s focus is on mapping relationships and testing a hypothesized mediation structure, so the extraction leaves ml_techniques empty and main_findings as an empty array.
